name: EGLE MiEnviro CSO/SSO List (sewage discharge reports: CSO, SSO, RTB and other discharges)
operator: Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE), Water Resources Division
waters_covered: statewide; every sewer system subject to MCL 324.3112a
access_detail: Public AngularJS page (MiEnviro, Windsor Solutions nCORE) 'CSO and SSO Information in MiEnviro', linked from Michigan.gov/SewageDischarge. It calls an unauthenticated JSON service: GET https://mienviro.michigan.gov/ncore/ss/ssolist?queryParams=<url-encoded JSON {filter:[{...}],top:2001}>. Filter keys seen in the app: reportStatusId (IN_PROCESS | COMPLETE), responsiblePartyName, siteName, permitNumber, submissionReferenceNumber (wildcards /%x/%), eventStartDateMin/Max, eventEndDateMin/Max, receivingWater, countyDescription. Lookups at /ncore/ss/ssolistlookups (default filter IN_PROCESS); per-record detail at /ncore/ss/ssodetails/?queryParams={filter:[{submissionId,sectionNumber}]} (same fields, no coordinates). The page's own 'Download CSV' uses the same service. An unfiltered query timed out at 60 s; filtered queries return in seconds. Fetched 2026-11-03: IN_PROCESS 332 rows (82 KB gz); COMPLETE with start >= 2026-10-01: 78 rows (CSO 56, RTB 12, SSO 7, other 3).

sample_record.deqActions: Long-term Control Program being implemented; controls include retention/treatment basins (6 on-line), CSO Screening/Disi ...

cadence: Rows appear when the operator submits the initial notice (statute: 'immediately, but not more than 24 hours after the discharge begins'). In the 332 in-process rows, submissionReceivedDate minus eventStartDate had median 20.7 h, 10th percentile 1.4 h, 90th percentile 134 h. Initial rows carry start (often end = start), type and quality but no volume; volume, end time, receiving water and feature number arrive when the report is completed and status changes to COMPLETE.
history: System holds records back to 2001 (some 2001 rows still IN_PROCESS); one row has a typo year 3021. Annual CSO/SSO/RTB report PDFs 2019-2021 on the EGLE page.
license: No licence or terms statement found on the list page; michigan.gov footer 'Copyright 2026 State of Michigan'. Public statutory posting (MCL 324.3112a(2)).
legal_basis: MCL 324.3112a(1)-(2); 40 CFR 122.38 (GLWA and other CSO permittees designate this list as their 4-hour public notice)
status_reason: Statewide, event-level, machine-readable, public: the feed to build first. Needs join to EPA inventory for coordinates (permitNumber + featureNumber).
notes: dischargeType/dischargeQuality values are doubled ('CSO Discharge,CSO Discharge'); one submission can hold several sections (outfalls) sharing submissionReferenceNumber (e.g. HQS-P25H-0AHKY with sections 2,3,4); stable key = id (Int64 as string) or submissionReferenceNumber+sectionNumber. GLWA's initial rows had no permitNumber or receivingWater. SSO rows use state permit-like ids '3112a-0707'. Timestamps carry offsets (-04:00/-05:00).

name: MCL 324.3112a (NREPA Part 31): discharge of untreated or partially treated sewage; notice, posting, E. coli testing
waters_covered: all waters of the state and land
access_detail: Statute text fetched (raw/mcl-324-3112a.html). History: 1994 Act 451; am. 1998 Act 3; 2000 Act 286; 2004 Act 72.
status_reason: Primary legal basis: 24-hour notice to EGLE, local health departments and daily newspapers; EGLE must post on its website; E. coli testing of affected waters.
notes: (1) '...the person responsible for the sewer system shall immediately, but not more than 24 hours after the discharge begins, notify the department; local health departments ...; a daily newspaper of general circulation in the county or counties in which a municipality notified pursuant to subsection (4) is located; and a daily newspaper of general circulation in the county in which the discharge occurred or is occurring...' (2) 'Upon being notified of a discharge under subsection (1), the department shall promptly post the notification on its website.' (3) test affected waters for E. coli, up to 10 tests per event, results to county health departments and EGLE (waivable by the health department). (4) annual contact of downstream municipalities, which may opt in to the same notice.

name: EGLE BeachGuard (MiEnviro nSITE beach explorer)
access_detail: React app; POST https://mienviro.michigan.gov/nsite/ss/explorersites with JSON {insertUpdateList:[{displayHeight,displayWidth,filterValuesJson:null,isIncludeUnmappable,latitudeMin/Max,longitudeMin/Max,modeId:'BEACH',searchTerm:''}]} and headers Origin/Referer from the site (without Referer it returns 400). Statewide extent returns clusters (totalSiteCount 2913); a small bbox returns sites: id, siteId, siteName, geographyWKT POINT, color (#188018 no advisory, #AAAAAA no data; red closed, yellow advisory per EGLE). Advisory detail endpoints (beachadvisories, beachresults) need login (401). Mode settings at /nsite/api/settings/getWslSettings?environment=beach.
cadence: Local health departments enter results; EGLE says advisories/closures 'within 24 hours' of an exceedance; weekly sampling Memorial Day to Labor Day.
legal_basis: BEACH Act; Michigan Part 31 water quality standard (E. coli 300/100 mL daily geometric mean, 130/100 mL 30-day)
status_reason: Statewide current status with points; history and reasons need the logged-in detail or snapshots.
notes: Status colour includes green for 'no advisory'; the site must not map that to green (grey = no report).
